focus: Landmine: looks like 'one time that' but uma vez que = 'once/given that' - causal-temporal, not counting times.
English 'as' trap: a medida que is the proportional 'as' (the more X, the more Y), not 'como'.
Literal hook: ou seja = 'or be it' (seja is subjunctive of ser), frozen into 'in other words'.
English packs the habit into the adverb 'usually'; Portuguese uses a verb: costuma acordar = 'is in the habit of waking'.
Literal hook: volta e meia = 'a turn and a half' - every so often.
Landmine: gata is literally 'cat' - calling someone a cat means they're hot.
Quote the card ('Que ele faca'): que + subjunctive opens a wish/command = 'let him', with no word for 'let'.
Give the contrast: insistir que + indicative asserts a fact; subjunctive would turn it into a demand for action.
One rule only: raiz is literally 'root' - rootsy/authentic, no frills; cut the second gloss (frescura).
Literal hook: show de bola = 'a show of ball(-play)' - a football spectacle turned all-purpose praise.
Literal hook: pao-duro is literally 'hard bread' = a tightwad.
Hook on mandar: literally 'send the real (one)' - mandar fronts many speech commands (manda ver).
Hook: partiu is literally past tense 'departed' - 'we're off' used to mean 'let's go'.
Reusable chunk: dar conta de = to handle/manage; recado is the errand you deliver on.
Literal hook: corda is a wind-up spring - com a corda toda = fully wound up.
Grammar gem: the -ao augmentative - ligeiro (quick) + -ao = 'a real quick one'; works on many adjectives.
Fact hook: a menina dos olhos is literally the pupil of the eye - same image as English 'apple of the eye'.
One rule only: cara is literally 'face' - Brazil's all-purpose 'dude'; cut the second gloss (irada).
Literal hook: osso = 'bone' - ta osso = it's tough.
One rule only: vacilo, from vacilar (cognate 'vacillate') - hesitation turned blunder; cut the Po gloss.
